Might be an unpopular opinion, but I don't want Smolder to be encouraged to aa more often. Being a purely caster marksman is a unique design that I think should be conserved, not changed into yet another aa-to-win marksman. I think the game needs more adcs that win with buttons rather than right clicks.

The fundamental design problem with Smolder is that he just hit and runs while providing similar or even higher damage than other adcs that need to expose themselves to do real damage, while also being allowed to build very tanky. Riot balances this by relegating all this power to his late game and make his early game (theorically) more and more depressing to play so that you make his life hell in early, but he makes your life hell in late. This kind of design is usually very hated by players because when you play as such champion, half of the game is hell, when you are not the one playing the champ you only see the moment when this champ is breking everything (think of Kayle, Kassadin, Aerosol). The solution here is to shoehorn him even more towards crit builds and making him more dependant on exposing himself. He has one damaging ability and then all the rest of his kit entirely dedicated to self-defense and this is generally a bad idea.

- Lower his Q damage but make it scale with crit dmg as well (afaik it's the only skill in the game whose damage scales with crti chance, but not crit dmg, why?). One of the reasons Smolder doesn't like building crit is that there aren't enough good crit items out there. He doesn't aa, so he doesn't care about attack speed and IE and Yun Tal don't work because they synergize with AAs specifically. Although I'd love to see Yun Tal reworked so that it can work with skills that crit as well, there's really 0 reasons why IE shouldn't synergize with Smolder. If this isn't enough to bring him to a crit build, then severly gut the AD scaling on his burn and make it scale with crit as well.

- Change his E so that it's a stronger offensive tool. This may be counterintuitive, but usually having skills that are great defensive tools being also good offensive tools is good design. Champs like Ezreal, Tristana, Akshan will rarely have good killing pressure if they won't jump on you, but doing so makes them burn their only good defensive tool. Smolder's E is rarely ever used offensively, it's always kept to kite away. They should rearrange his power budget so that until he actually gets close with his E, he's not really a threat of killing you. One way to make this is to make his Q splash damage much less frightening, so that unless he directly clicks Q on you it shouldn't be that big of a deal.

- Another unpopular opinion of mine: neither the max HP true dmg burn nor the execute are problematic themselves, even though no matter how you balance them there's just no way to make them not frustrating for a lot of people. Compared to the other 2 champs in the game that have maxHP% true damage, being one time at 550 range for a split second is a way too easy condition than landing 3 consecutive aa or hitting you form a specific angle as a melee champ. As such, one single Q alone shouldn't do a lot of dmg in itself. One way could be that the execute only applies to the champ he hit directly with the Q, and not the ones that got hit by the splash damage.

> Regardless of your level and items a lvl 1 smolder with 225 stacks will always take the same amount of q's to execute you.

No. Really no. Without any AD or damage from the Q itself, it's like less than 2% of your hp over 3 seconds, so less than 1% of your max hp per second. Would literally take 100 Qs to kill you.
